label: 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tube
description: Spun in a microcentrifuge in adapters.

label: Beaker
description: Graduations are approximate (about ±5 %); never a measuring device for quantitative work.

label: Volumetric flask (class A)
description: Make up to the mark; not for adding a measured volume.

references: ISO 1042:1998 Laboratory glassware: one-mark volumetric flasks (class A tolerances)

label: Measuring cylinder (class B)
description: Adequate for approximate volumes; not for analytical work.

references: ISO 4788:2005 Laboratory glassware: graduated measuring cylinders (class B)

label: Polystyrene semi-micro cuvette, 1 cm
description: Opaque below about 340 nm: use quartz for UV work.

label: Polystyrene macro cuvette, 1 cm
description: For 3 mL reactions started and mixed in the cell. Opaque below about 340 nm.

label: Quartz micro-cuvette, 1 cm
description: For UV readings of small volumes (column fractions).

label: 96-well plate, clear flat bottom
description: Absorbance path length depends on the volume in each well (V / well area).

label: 96-well ELISA plate, high-binding
description: Absorbance path length depends on the volume in each well (V / well area).

label: 96-well PCR plate, white, with optical seal
description: Thin-walled wells for fast heating; white walls reflect the fluorescence up to the reader.

label: Aqueous waste (sink, with plenty of water)
Sharps bin (yellow)
description: For used needles and syringes, as they are: never resheath a needle.

label: Variable single-channel air-displacement micropipette
description: Error tables are typical manufacturer-style values at 10 %, 50 % and 100 % of nominal volume; ISO 8655-2 maximum permissible errors bound them.

references: ISO 8655-2:2022 Piston-operated volumetric apparatus, part 2: piston pipettes

label: Glass Pasteur pipette with teat
description: For adding a liquid dropwise (about 20 drops to the millilitre): volumes are approximate.

label: Syringe with needle
description: A disposable syringe on a long needle: it draws liquid through a septum and delivers it into a sealed flask. Flushed with nitrogen first, it carries no air in. Single use: into the sharps bin, never resheathed.

label: 1 mL syringe and needle (graduated in 0.01 mL)
Nitrogen balloon on a needle
description: A balloon filled from the nitrogen line, on a needle. Through a septum with a vent needle beside it, it flushes the air out of a flask; left in, it keeps the flask under nitrogen as liquid is drawn out.

references: ISO 648:2008 Laboratory glassware: single-volume pipettes (class A)

label: Semi-micro balance (0.01 mg)
description: What ISO 8655 asks for when checking pipettes at 10 to 100 µL.

provenance.notes: Generic teaching-lab instrument; stray-light fraction and noise are typical orders of magnitude.

label: pH meter with combination electrode
description: Uncalibrated, the display is off by a few tenths of a pH unit and slightly compressed; a two-point calibration fixes both.

label: Platinum redox electrode with Ag/AgCl reference (mV meter)
description: Reads the potential a redox couple sets on platinum, against a silver chloride reference (+0.21 V against the hydrogen electrode). A solution with no couple gives a wandering reading.

label: Centrifuge
description: Rotor positions are numbered from 1; tubes opposite each other must match in mass.

label: Microcentrifuge, 24 × 1.5/2 mL
description: Takes 0.2 mL PCR tubes in adapters too.

label: Benchtop centrifuge, swing-out rotor, 4 × 15/50 mL
description: Speeds in rpm convert through its 11 cm rotor radius (3000 rpm is about 1100 × g). Load opposite buckets with matching tubes.

label: Inoculating loop
description: A wire loop that picks up a small, imprecise volume. It is its own tip: it carries a film from whatever it last touched until it is flamed.

provenance.notes: Calibrated loops hold about 10 µL; the volume varies by about half with technique.

label: Light microscope
description: Shows the shapes, arrangements and colours of cells on a slide, never what they are.

label: Compound microscope, bright field and phase contrast (4×–100× oil)
description: Binocular, 10× eyepieces (field number 18). Condenser turret: bright field, Ph1 for the 10× and Ph2 for the 40× objective. Its controls stay as they are set (core:configure, core:focus).

label: Prepared slide
description: A specimen fixed, stained and mounted under a coverslip: its `specimen` names what there is to see.

label: Prepared slide: stained stem, transverse section
Prepared slide: printed letter e
description: For seeing which way round the image is.

label: Prepared slide: root tip squash (mitosis)
description: A stained, mounted specimen ready to look at.

label: Prepared slide: leaf lower epidermis (impression)
description: A stained, mounted specimen ready to look at.

label: Prepared slide: leaf upper epidermis (impression)
description: A stained, mounted specimen ready to look at.

label: Prepared slide: lily anther (meiosis)
description: A stained, mounted specimen ready to look at.

label: 10 mL dropper bottle
description: Dispenses drops of about 30 µL: pour from it.

label: Filter funnel with paper
description: Gravity filtration through fluted paper: slow, and the cake stays wetter.

provenance.notes: A vacuum-filtered crystalline cake holds roughly its own mass of liquid.

label: Melting-point apparatus
description: Heats a capillary of sample slowly; the learner reads where it starts to melt and where it is clear.

label: Dissolved-oxygen meter
description: A probe dipped into a liquid reads its dissolved oxygen in mg/L (air-saturated water: about 9 mg/L at room temperature).

label: FTIR spectrometer (ATR)
description: A little of the sample pressed on the ATR crystal gives its infrared spectrum: % transmittance from 4000 to 600 cm⁻¹, and the bands picked out (s, m, w; br for broad). Carbonyls near 1650-1800, O–H and N–H broad near 2500-3500.

label: Electrospray mass spectrometer
description: A few microlitres infused into an electrospray source in positive or negative ion mode: the peaks (m/z, intensity relative to the base peak). Proteins sprayed from acidic aqueous acetonitrile carry a broad envelope of charges.

label: Fluorimeter (scanning)
description: Excites a quartz cuvette at one wavelength and scans the emitted light at right angles: an emission spectrum in counts. Too concentrated a sample absorbs its own light (the inner filter effect): keep absorbance at the excitation below about 0.1.

label: Chromatography system with UV monitor
description: Pumps buffer through a column at 0.5 mL/min from a 500 µL injection loop; a 2 mm flow cell after the column records the absorbance at 280 and 254 nm against the volume passed.

label: Rotary evaporator
description: Turns a round-bottom flask in a 40 °C bath under reduced pressure: ethyl acetate, ethanol and the like distil off in minutes, water left as a layer of its own only slowly.

label: Agar plate (90 mm Petri dish)
description: A poured agar plate: its preparation is the medium. Liquid put on it soaks in; cells stay on the surface and grow into colonies.

label: Cell spreader (L-shaped, glass)
description: Dipped in ethanol and flamed between plates; otherwise it carries cells from one plate to the next.

label: Forceps (fine-tipped)
description: For handling discs: dipped in ethanol, the ethanol burnt off in the flame, then cooled a few seconds before use.

label: Test tube (glass, 16 × 150 mm)
description: For small-scale tests: a few millilitres of solution and drops of reagent. Hold it to the light to see colours and precipitates.

label: Boiling tube (glass, 25 × 150 mm)
description: A wide tube for heating, or for more liquid than a test tube holds.

label: Gas syringe
description: A glass syringe whose plunger is pushed out by the gas a reaction gives off.

label: Flame-test wire (nichrome loop in a handle)
description: Cleaned by dipping in concentrated hydrochloric acid and heating until it gives the flame no colour; otherwise it shows what it last held.

label: Gas syringe (100 mL, glass)
description: Graduated every 1 mL to 100 mL; fitted to a bung in the reaction flask.

label: Photosynthometer (capillary gas collector)
description: Gas from a plant in water collects in a flared tube and is drawn into a capillary, where its length is read against a scale: about 0.01 mL resolution, up to 20 mL.

label: Digital voltmeter (high resistance)
description: Two leads: red (+) and black (−). It draws almost no current, so it reads the cell’s full potential difference to 1 mV. Across two vessels it needs a salt bridge to complete the circuit.

label: Conductivity meter (temperature-compensated)
description: A cell of two electrodes dipped into the liquid: its conductivity in µS/cm (mS/cm above 2000), corrected to 25 °C, and the total dissolved solids it implies (0.64 mg/L per µS/cm). Rinse it with deionised water between samples.

label: Low-voltage DC power supply with ammeter
description: Up to 12 V and 3 A, with the current set by a knob and read on its ammeter. Through a poorly conducting liquid it cannot reach the set current.

label: Glass gas syringe, 100 mL, with a sealed nozzle
description: Draw in air and cap the nozzle: the trapped gas can be squeezed or warmed, its volume read on the barrel to 0.5 mL, and liquid injected through the cap with a hypodermic syringe. The plunger moves freely (so the gas stays at atmospheric pressure) unless held.

label: Pressure sensor (data logger)
description: Connected to a sealed syringe by a short tube: the gas pressure in kPa, to 0.1 kPa.

label: Ruler (30 cm)
description: Held over a tray of water to measure the diameter of a film on its surface.

label: Ripple tray (30 × 40 cm)
description: A shallow tray of clean water, its surface dusted with lycopodium powder so that a film spreading on it pushes the powder back into a clear circle.

label: Ice–salt freezing mixture (about −18 °C)
description: Crushed ice stirred with a third of its mass of salt in a beaker: a slushy liquid at about −18 °C that takes heat quickly from a tube stood in it.

label: Simple respirometer (boiling tube, capillary and scale)
description: A boiling tube sealed by a bung carrying a capillary with a drop of coloured liquid: as the gas inside shrinks or grows the drop moves along the scale, read as the volume of gas to 0.001 mL. Organisms sit on a gauze above soda lime (or none), and a screw clip lets air in to reset it.

label: Vacuum flask (500 mL), plugged with cotton wool
description: Double-walled with a vacuum between the walls: heat leaks out about a hundred times more slowly than from an open beaker. The cotton-wool plug lets air in for respiration.

label: Fly culture vial with food and a foam bung
description: A tube with a layer of fly food and a foam bung. Kept at 25 °C, a pair of flies leaves its offspring in about ten days; clear the parents after seven so they are not counted with them.

label: Hand lens and white tile (etherised flies)
description: Flies knocked out with ether (or carbon dioxide) are tipped onto a white tile, sorted with a fine brush and counted by sex and appearance.

label: Choice chamber (two-sided)
description: A shallow dish divided under a gauze floor into two halves: put silica gel (dry) or damp paper (humid) under each half, and cover a half with black card to darken it. Animals go in through the centre of the lid.

label: Electrode on a crocodile-clip lead
description: Clip a metal strip or a graphite rod into it (add the electrode as a solid). Unclip the electrode to weigh it: the balance weighs only what the clip holds.

label: Potometer (bubble potometer, 1 mm capillary)
description: A water-filled tube with a leafy shoot sealed into one end and a capillary at the other. As the shoot takes up water an air bubble moves along the capillary; its scale reads the volume taken up to 0.001 mL (about 1.3 mm of the capillary). A reservoir resets the bubble.

label: BOD bottle (300 mL, ground-glass stopper)
description: Filled to overflowing and stoppered with no bubble, it holds water out of contact with the air, so its dissolved oxygen changes only by what lives in it.

label: Plant growth cabinet (lit, temperature-controlled)
description: Fluorescent tubes give about 250 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹; the air is held at a set temperature and about 50 % relative humidity.

label: Culture tube with cap (glass, 20 mL)
description: For broths. Flame the neck when it is opened and before it is closed.

label: Agar deep (narrow tube of set agar)
description: Stab it with a loaded loop: where growth appears along the stab shows the organism's oxygen requirement.

label: Agar slope (slant) in a universal
description: A culture kept on a slope of agar; take cells from it with a loop.

label: Looking (against the light)
description: What the eye sees: whether a broth is clear or cloudy, where an agar deep has grown, the colonies on a plate by their look.

label: Antibiotic susceptibility disc (6 mm)
description: A paper disc carrying a stated mass of one antibiotic; pressed onto a seeded plate, the drug diffuses out into the agar.

label: Sterile blank filter-paper disc (13 mm)
description: A blank paper disc that soaks up about 50 µL: wet it with a test solution, then lay it on a seeded plate.

label: Zone ruler (millimetres)
description: Read against a dark background from the back of the plate: the diameter of the clear zone, the disc included, to the nearest millimetre.

label: UV lamp (long-wave)
description: Wear UV-protective glasses.

label: Agarose gel
description: A cast gel with ten wells in one row and a DNA stain in the agarose. Lane n is well An.

label: SDS-polyacrylamide gel
description: A precast mini gel with ten wells in one row, run in SDS buffer; its stain-free imaging shows protein bands from about 20 ng. Lane n is well An.

label: 4-20 % gradient SDS-polyacrylamide gel, 10 wells (pre-cast)
description: A gradient gel resolves a wider range than one percentage; its mobility is taken as a 12 % gel's. Stained with Coomassie: a band shows from about 50 ng and stays roughly proportional to a few micrograms.

label: Size-exclusion column
description: A packed gel-filtration bed. Put the sample on the bed, then collect fractions as running buffer is pushed through: large molecules leave first.

label: Size-exclusion column, 24 mL bed (5–250 kDa)
description: Void volume 8.0 mL (measured with blue dextran), total bed volume 24 mL.

label: Analytical size-exclusion column, 10 × 300 mm (1-1300 kDa)
description: A high-resolution gel-filtration column for a chromatography system: void volume 8 mL, total volume 24 mL, run at 0.5 mL/min.

label: Desalting column, 8.5 mL bed (excludes above 5 kDa)
description: Proteins leave in the void volume; salts and small molecules come later.

label: Pasteur-pipette column of CM-Sephadex G-50 (about 2 mL bed)
description: A glass Pasteur pipette plugged with glass wool and packed with CM-Sephadex G-50 to 1-1.5 cm from the top. The beads sieve by size (1.5-30 kDa) and carry carboxymethyl groups, negative above about pH 4: in a weak buffer they hold positively charged molecules and push negative ones out of their pores; a strong buffer swamps both.

label: TLC plate, silica gel with F254 indicator (5 × 7 cm, 5 lanes)
description: Pencil the origin 1 cm from the bottom. Spots show as dark patches under 254 nm light, where they quench the indicator.

label: TLC developing chamber with lid
description: Keep the eluent below the plate's origin: about 20 mL per centimetre of depth.

label: UV lamp (long-wave, 365 nm)
description: For fluorescence (GFP, fluorescent dyes). Wear UV-protective glasses.

label: UV lamp (short-wave, 254 nm)
description: For TLC plates with a fluorescent indicator. Wear UV-protective glasses.

label: Digital thermometer (0.1 °C)
description: Reads the liquid it dips into; its small calibration offset cancels in a temperature change.

label: Polystyrene-cup calorimeter with lid
description: Two nested polystyrene cups with a lid: heat leaks out about 25 times more slowly than from a beaker.

label: Nickel affinity column, 1 mL bed (His-tag)
description: Nickel resin holds His-tagged proteins (about 40 mg per mL of bed) until imidazole displaces them; other proteins stick only weakly.

label: Nitrocellulose membrane in a tray (6 × 8 cm)
description: Binds any protein that touches it until blocked: block before the antibodies go on.

label: 6 % native polyacrylamide gel, 10 wells (for gel shifts)
description: No SDS: proteins keep their shape, so a protein bound to DNA runs with it as a shifted band. Image labelled DNA on a fluorescence imager.

label: Gel imager (blue-light transilluminator)
description: Shows stained bands; sizes come from comparison with a ladder.

label: Fluorescence gel imager
description: Sees only labelled molecules (a fluorescent probe), about a hundred times more sensitively than a stain, and integrates each band.

label: 250 mL round-bottom flask (distillation pot)
description: With anti-bumping granules, a heating mantle, a still head with thermometer and a condenser.

label: 100 mL round-bottom flask (single neck)
description: With a stirrer bar: for a reaction heated under reflux, and for taking the solvent off on the rotary evaporator.

label: 250 mL separating funnel
description: With a stopper and a tap, in a ring on a stand. Stoppered, it is shaken (venting often) to bring two liquids that do not mix to equilibrium; the layers settle and the lower one runs off through the tap, the stopper out.

label: Vigreux fractionating column (about 3 theoretical plates)
description: Fitted between the flask and the still head: the vapour condenses and re-boils on its indentations, a few equilibrium stages in all.

label: Gel imager (blue-light transilluminator)
description: Shows where the stained bands are; sizes come from comparison with a ladder.

label: Sanger sequencing (service)
description: Reads the DNA in a sample (a PCR product): up to about 1000 bases of the template it mostly holds. Too little DNA gives no readable trace; two templates give double peaks.

label: Haemocytometer (improved Neubauer) with coverslip
description: Each large corner square holds 0.1 µL (1 mm × 1 mm × 0.1 mm): cells per square × 10⁴ = cells per mL.

label: Bench (room temperature)
description: Open benches: about 0.5 airborne organisms settle per cm² per hour on anything uncovered (a teaching lab in use).

label: Heating mantle with stirrer and reflux condenser
description: The flask sits in a heating mantle on a stirrer with a water-cooled condenser in its neck: the mixture boils at its own boiling point and the condensed vapour runs back, so nothing boils away however long it refluxes.

label: Hot plate
description: Above 100 °C an aqueous solution boils: it stays at 100 °C and loses solvent.

label: Lamp (bench lamp with an LED bulb)
description: What stands in front of it is lit by about 1600 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ at 10 cm, falling as the square of the distance; an LED gives little heat. What it lights stands in a beaker of water (a heat shield) whose temperature can be set. A coloured filter can go in front.

label: Dark cupboard
description: No light: for dark controls (or wrap a tube in foil).

label: Ice–water bath
description: Ice with water around a flask: cools faster than a bucket of crushed ice.

label: Thermal cycler, 96 × 0.2 mL tubes (end-point)
description: Runs a PCR program on tubes; the products are looked at afterwards, on a gel.

label: Real-time PCR cycler (96-well plate)
description: Reads every well through the lid after each cycle; its software subtracts each well's baseline and reports the cycle where the signal crosses the threshold (Cq), and can run a melt curve.

label: Cooled incubator
description: A refrigerated (BOD) incubator: it holds temperatures below room temperature too.

label: Freezer (−20 °C)
description: Long-term storage of enzymes, DNA and finished PCRs.
